business_problem: Wealthsimple needed a standardized way to deploy and serve machine-learning models for fraud, transaction routing, onboarding, and personalization, but framework-specific inference stacks were taking months to ship and causing outages that hurt customer transfers.
solution_summary: Wealthsimple turned its fragmented model-serving environment into an internal ML-as-a-service platform by standardizing on NVIDIA Triton Inference Server and GPU-backed deployment on AWS. Triton replaced bespoke, framework-specific servers with a single inference layer that could run on both CPUs and GPUs, while A10G instances and the NVIDIA GPU-Optimized AWS Machine Image gave the company a repeatable runtime for production serving. On top of that platform, Wealthsimple now runs more than 30 models across fraud detection, suspicious-transaction analysis, customer recommendations, onboarding, and institutional-transfer routing. Because the serving layer is standardized, model developers can deploy without waiting on a separate engineering team, and the platform organization can focus on shared reliability and cost tuning instead of one-off integrations for each model family.

solution_components.name: NVIDIA AI Enterprise

data_flow: Feature data from onboarding, transaction, and recommendation workflows flows into models served by Triton on A10G-backed AWS environments. Predictions are returned to Wealthsimple's product systems for fraud detection, transfer routing, and personalization, while the shared platform lets new models move into production without bespoke serving work.
business_outcome: Wealthsimple reduced model delivery time from months to under 15 minutes, raised inference uptime from 95 percent to 99.999 percent, cut serving latency by 20 percent, and delivered 145 million predictions over 12 months with no IT tickets tied to AI inferencing.
